case_title: Shyamal Ghosh v. State of West Bengal
accused_victim_relationship: Prior dispute/extortion: accused demanded Rs.40,000 ('Tola Mastani Salami') over the victim's shop rooms and threatened him; no family or personal relationship stated.
statutory_provisions: IPC s.302, s.201, s.379, s.411 read with s.34
weapon: Sharp cutting weapon (chopper) for dismemberment; gumcha used for strangulation
evidence_type: Eyewitness testimony; circumstantial (last seen together); recovery of weapon, van and cycle; medical (post-mortem); documentary (FIR, post-mortem report, seizure memos)
confession: Admission by accused Bishu leading to recovery of the chopper; the Court relied on the recovery, not on the admission as a confession.
aggravating_circumstances: Brutal killing and dismemberment of the body; threats and extortion demand; absconding for days together
trial_court_outcome: Convicted of all charges (ss.302, 201, 379, 411 r/w s.34); death sentence under s.302; s.201 seven years RI and fine; s.379 three years and fine
high_court_outcome: Death reference answered in negative; s.379/34 acquittal; s.302/34 conviction maintained with life imprisonment and Rs.5,000 fine; s.201/34 sentence maintained
offence_finally_established: IPC s.302 read with s.34 (murder); IPC s.201 read with s.34 (disappearance of evidence)
neutral_facts: The victim had constructed shop rooms on his own land for letting out. A group of men demanded Rs. 40,000 from him as a payment connected with the construction and threatened him with dire consequences if it was not paid. The threats were repeated over several weeks, including at the victim's house, and on 27 September the group said they would murder him if the money was not paid within a day. On the night of 29 September the victim left home on his bicycle to collect money from a business contact and set out for home around 11 p.m. Near a field on his route he was stopped by a group of men and an altercation followed. Eyewitnesses saw several of the accused strangle him with a gumcha. The body was then cut into pieces with a sharp cutting weapon and packed into gunny bags. On the following evening, witnesses saw several of the accused loading the gunny bags into a steel-coloured Maruti van at a rickshaw stand. Two gunny bags containing body parts were later found by a passer-by, who reported them to the police. The victim's wife and brother lodged a missing diary report and later identified the body. The van driver was arrested and the van was recovered on his statement. The victim's bicycle and a chopper were recovered on the statements of accused persons. Post-mortem found death due to ligature strangulation and that all body parts belonged to one person. Several accused absconded for a long period and were arrested later from other places. At identification, eyewitnesses identified all the accused in court, while the van driver did not identify one accused.
physical_harm: Death by strangulation by ligature; body severed into multiple pieces (head, limbs, torso)
number_of_offences: 4 charged; 2 finally upheld (s.302/34 and s.201/34); s.379 acquitted by High Court; s.411 not separately addressed by the Supreme Court
financial_property_loss: Victim's cash, four rings and HMT watch with him (reported by witness); extortion demand of Rs.40,000 (not paid)
premeditation_planning: Court found common intention to do away with the victim if the Rs.40,000 demand was not met; no express finding of premeditated planning beyond this
motive: Illegal demand of Rs.40,000 coupled with threats of dire consequences (accepted by the Court)
key_evidence_accepted: Eyewitnesses PW8, PW17, PW19 (altercation and strangulation); PW7, PW9, PW11 (loading of gunny bags into van); PW16 post-mortem; recoveries of chopper, van and cycle; last seen together evidence
witness_credibility: Eyewitnesses found reliable and trustworthy; related witnesses (PW2, PW4, PW6) not rejected mechanically; hostile witnesses PW13 and PW23 relied on only to extent they support prosecution; minor timing variations not material
post_offence_conduct: Absconded immediately after the occurrence for days together, arrested later from Delhi and Sodhpur; one accused admitted absconding and surrendered after charges were framed
trial_duration: offence: 29th/30th September, 2003 (midnight); trial judgment: 13 September 2005; High Court: 5 February 2007; Supreme Court: 11 July 2012
legal_representation: Counsel listed collectively for the appearing parties; the judgment does not separate counsel for the accused and for the State
investigation_status: FIR registered (Case No. 332/03); investigation completed; charge sheet filed against six accused, two absconders later arrested and charged; trial completed
procedural_irregularity: Investigation lapses: no FSL submission of gunny bags and weapons, no photographs or site plan; delay of 3 to 20 days in recording some witness statements; no test identification parade success for one accused
appeal_history: Trial court: convicted, death sentence. High Court: s.379/34 acquitted, s.302/34 life imprisonment, death reference answered in negative. Supreme Court: appeals dismissed.
prosecution_argument: Clear motive of demand of money; eyewitnesses reliable; absconding and s.313 statements support prosecution; hostile witnesses and investigation defects do not help accused; s.34 ingredients satisfied
defence_argument: Circumstantial chain incomplete; hostile witnesses PW13 and PW23; eyewitnesses PW8, PW17, PW19 did not name accused and were tutored or chance witnesses; delay in recording statements; no test identification parade identification; no common intention for s.34
legal_principle_applied: Last seen together theory and shifting of onus; s.34 IPC common intention and participation; contradiction and omission test; hostile witness principle; test identification parade as corroboration; defects in investigation not fatal
precedent_relied_upon: Govindaraju v. State (2012) 4 SCC 122; Brathi v. State of Punjab (1991) 1 SCC 519; Banti v. State of M.P. (2004) 1 SCC 414; State of U.P. v. Satish (2005) 3 SCC 114; S.K. Yusuf v. State of West Bengal (2011) 11 SCC 754; Mohd. Azad v. State of W.B. (2008) 15 SCC 449; Mahender Singh Dahiya (2011) 3 SCC 109; Rabindra Kumar Pal v. Republic of India (2011) 2 SCC 490; Sunil Kumar Sambhudayal Gupta (2010) 13 SCC 657; Subhash v. State of Haryana (2011) 2 SCC 715; Tika Ram v. State of M.P. (2007) 15 SCC 760; C. Muniappan (2010) 9 SCC 567; Sheo Shankar Singh (2011) 3 SCC 654; Nand Kishore (2011) 12 SCC 120; Lallan Rai (2003) 1 SCC 268; Dharamidhar (2010) 7 SCC 759; Mousam Singha Roy (2003) 12 SCC 377
sentencing_rationale: Not applicable (appeals dismissed; Court saw no reason to interfere with High Court's sentence, without separate reasoning on sentence)
judicial_aggravating_factors: Brutal nature of the crime; dismemberment and disposal of body; absconding conduct

case_title.quote: SHYAMAL GHOSH v. STATE OF WEST BENGAL (Criminal Appeal No. 507 of 2007 etc.)

number_of_accused.quote: The present appeals were filed by four of the accused.

accused_gender.quote: Accused Ganesh, in his statement under Section 313 Cr.P.C., admitted the fact that he was absconding

victim_gender.quote: the victim Archideb Bhattacharjee had started from his house on his Avon bicycle

accused_victim_relationship.quote: The accused persons had then threatened him with dire consequences.

offence_category.quote: For killing one person and disposing of the body, after cutting it, in gunny bags

statutory_provisions.quote: The accused were charged u/ss. 302, 201, 379, 411 rlw. s. 34 IPC.

weapon.quote: severed the head, legs, hands and body of the corpse by a sharp cutting weapon and after putting the same in gunny bags

evidence_type.quote: There are eye-witnesses who had seen the scuffling between the deceased and the accused and the strangulation of the deceased

confession.quote: recovered on the statement of accused Bishu who brought out the chopper from the bush in the field and admitted that they had cut the body of the deceased with the chopper

aggravating_circumstances.quote: the present case is not a case where the accused were innocent

trial_court_outcome.quote: awarded sentence of death to all the accused persons for the offence under Section 302 IPC

high_court_outcome.quote: while answering the death reference in the negative, acquitted all the accused persons of the offence under Section 379 read with Section 34 IPC

imprisonment_type.quote: the Court awarded them rigorous imprisonment for life and to pay a fine of Rs.5,000/- each

fine_rs.quote: the Court awarded them rigorous imprisonment for life and to pay a fine of Rs.5,000/- each

neutral_facts.quote: The accused persons demanded Rs. 40,000 from the victim towards a 'Tola Mastani Salami' for the construction of shops. The victim refused and was threatened.

attempt_completion.quote: The accused killed him by strangulation.

physical_harm.quote: The cause of death was due to effect of strangulation by ligature.

number_of_offences.quote: The accused were charged u/ss. 302, 201, 379, 411 rlw. s. 34 IPC.

financial_property_loss.quote: according to PW4 the deceased was wearing four rings, HMT watch and was carrying cash and other papers with him

premeditation_planning.quote: all these acts obviously were in furtherance to the common intention of doing away with the deceased, if he failed to give them Rs. 40,000/- as demanded

motive.quote: one motive, i.e., illegal demand of money coupled with the warning of dire consequences to the deceased in case of default

key_evidence_accepted.quote: According to the prosecution, the statements of these witnesses completely establish that the deceased was last seen with the accused

witness_credibility.quote: Their statements are reliable and trustworthy.

post_offence_conduct.quote: The accused persons were absconding immediately after the date of the occurrence and could not be arrested despite various raids by the police authorities.

trial_duration.quote: On 1st October, 2003 ... The accused persons were absconding

legal_representation.quote: Pradip Ghosh, J.K. Das, Yadunandan Bansal, Rauf Rahim, Subhasish Bhowick, Tanmay K. Ghosh, Swati Yadav, P.P. Nayak

investigation_status.quote: Charge sheet against all other six accused was filed.

procedural_irregularity.quote: the Investigating Officer failed to send the blood stained gunny bags and other recovered weapons to the FSL, to take photographs of the shops in question, prepare the site plan thereof

appeal_history.quote: High Court maintained their conviction except u/s.379/34 IPC, answered the death reference in the negative and awarded R1 for life

prosecution_argument.quote: there existed a clear motive for committing the crime, i.e., demand of money

defence_argument.quote: The present case being a case of circumstantial evidence does not establish the complete chain of events

legal_principle_applied.quote: Once the last seen theory comes into play, the onus was on the accused to explain as to what happened to the deceased after they were together seen alive.

precedent_relied_upon.quote: statement of a hostile witness can also be relied upon by the Court to the extent it supports the case of the prosecution

sentencing_rationale.quote: we see no reason to interfere with the judgment of the High Court either on merits or on the quantum of sentence.

judicial_aggravating_factors.quote: all the three accused had a common intention in commission of this brutal crime
